task.note: 31 keys say sarcină, 19 under focusTask.* and plan.* say activitate for the same thing (focusTask.alert.deleteTask.title vs .message is one alert with both). restricted_list.note: Four shipped forms: blocate 1 (plan.createToDo.removeRestrictedApps), de restricții 2, restricționată 4, de aplicații restricționate 2. Chosen for plain wording: 'blocate' is what happens and 'Blocare aplicații' is already the welcome eyebrow. Alignment of the other 8 keys is a follow-up batch; the owner may flip this before the first ro batch. Apple's own Screen Time split confirms this reasoning: its app-limiting feature is named 'Limitare aplicații' (App Limits), not 'blocked'/'restricted' apps at all; 'Restricționat(e)' is reserved for Content & Privacy Restrictions and the generic OS-wide 'Blocat(e)' is the sense this term's 'blocate' sits closer to (cross-ref apple-ro-vocabulary.md, fetched 2026-09-16).

time_value_disclaimer.note: 10 keys vs 1 (widgets.monthlyTimeValue.description). The four sibling source sentences keep their own single ro form, listed in references/locale-briefs/ro.md '## Money frame'.

hourly_rate.note: 8 keys say tarif orar, 19 use tarif. One hit: screenTimeReport.missingWage 'câștigul pe oră', which is also a money-outcome word. No Apple or App Store equivalent exists for pricing a user's own time at their own rate; the closest competitor, I Am Sober, prices money saved by abstaining, a different frame from estimating income from focused time — this framing appears original to Moneyfesting, not a borrowed convention (store-ro-evidence.md, fetched 2026-09-16).

open.note: Archived guide section 7 prefers 'sesiune de focus'; the catalog has 3 keys with 'sesiune de focus' and 2 with 'sesiune de concentrare' (term_audit, snapshot 2026-09-15); across all ro copy the stem 'concentr*' appears in 72 keys against 'focus*' in 30 (whole-word 'focus' in 29); the same-source group 'Focus' renders as Focus (insights.focus.title, profile.sessionDetails.splitFocus) and Concentrare (profile.home.focusSection). Decide before the first ro batch; a flip is a global term change with its own follow-up batch, never a per-string choice. Harvest 2026-09-16 (iOS 26.1 (23B86) runtime: Applications/Preferences.app | Localizable.strings | Focus; System/Library/ControlCenter/Bundles/FocusUIModule.bundle | Localizable.strings | MODULE_DEFAULT_TITLE): iOS ro names the system Focus mode 'Concentrare', so the first half of the pre-registered rule holds. The second half does not: no key names the system mode, the app ships no Focus filter, iOS never says 'sesiune', and en already shares 'Focus' with the iOS mode, so ro carries the overlap en accepted. What changed: recommended_reason no longer carries the pending condition; recommended stays 'sesiune de concentrare'. The exact overlap is on bare labels, 'Concentrare' (profile.home.focusSection, en 'Focus') and 'Concentrare în desfășurare' (onboarding.welcome.preview.blocking.active); the owner may weigh that as confusion and flip. App Store evidence (store-ro-evidence.md, fetched 2026-09-16): Focus To-Do, one of the few Romanian-shipping focus-timer competitors, calls the same mechanic 'Temporizator Pomodoro' and the accumulated time 'timpul de concentrare' -- further competitor support for 'concentrare' over 'focus', though it uses neither word for the app-side 'sesiune' either; the recommendation is unchanged.

Recorded here so the divergence from Apple's own 'Premiu' (Fitness achievement icon) is not reopened blindly: Apple reserves 'Insignă' for the OS icon-decoration badge, a different UI object, and never uses it for an earned achievement icon. The counter-evidence stands as a documented, considered trade-off, not an oversight.
open.note: Disagreement from the Apple-Romanian vocabulary cross-reference (iOS 26.1 (23B86) runtime, fetched 2026-09-16: System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/ActivitySharingUI.framework | Localizable.strings | GENERIC_ACHIEVEMENT_NAME 'Premiu'; System/Library/CoreServices/MobileCoreTypes.bundle | InfoPlist.strings | Icon Decoration Badge 'Insignă'). Apple's own achievement system (Fitness) never uses 'insignă' for an earned achievement icon -- it says 'premiu' -- and reserves 'insignă' for a different UI object, the small icon-decoration badge (notification dot, lock, sync icon on an app icon). Keys: achievements.action.seeAllBadges, achievements.badgeUnlock.title, achievements.card.allEarned, achievements.gallery.earnedOfTotal, achievements.gallery.subtitle (5 keys, 'Insignă'/'Insigne' for the achievement concept); onboarding.notificationPermission.alertMessage also says 'insigne' but correctly in Apple's icon-decoration sense and is not part of this decision. Rule: a concept-vocabulary divergence from Apple's own nearest analog is an owner call, not a translation error, since 'insignă' is plain, understandable Romanian either way. Meanwhile the five keys stay locked and findings on them go to an audit scope the owner names; no App Store competitor evidence exists either way for this concept.
